clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: One-sample t-tests on deviation values; two-sample t-tests for between-group differences; Spearman's correlation for spatial similarity of group-average deviations; k-means and t-SNE for clustering; canonical correlation analysis (CCA) to link brain deviations with clinical/neuropsychological scores; partial least squares (PLS) regression and inter-regional similarity analysis to link brain deviations with gene expression profiles.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Young children with ASD show a common rightward gray matter volume asymmetry in the inferior parietal lobe and precentral gyrus, which is associated with ASD symptoms and underlying gene expression profiles, and is more severe in those with comorbid intellectual disability.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using a normative model on 1030 children, this study found a common pattern of rightward gray matter volume (GMV) asymmetry in the inferior parietal lobe and precentral gyrus, and higher variability in the temporal pole, across all ASD children. Children with ASD and comorbid DD/ID showed a more extensive abnormal pattern linked to both ASD symptoms and verbal IQ. Children with ASD but without DD/ID showed higher individual variability linked only to ASD symptoms. Children with only DD/ID showed no significant asymmetry differences from controls. These GMV laterality patterns were significantly associated with both shared and unique gene expression profiles, suggesting brain asymmetry is a potential mediator in the multiscale pathophysiology of developmental disorders.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. Reliance on VBM, which is sensitive to segmentation and registration accuracy. 2. Normative model only included age and sex, omitting environmental factors. 3. Association of child brain data with adult gene expression atlases. 4. Unbalanced sex ratio in the sample.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Some limitations of this study should be stated. Firstly, it is worth noting that GMV in current study is obtained by automated morphology method called voxel-based morphometry (VBM). ... Secondly, the normative model extracting GMV asymmetry deviations only considered the effects of age and sex. Environmental factors, such as socioeconomic status, may also affect the brain morphology development ... Thirdly, limited by the availability of gene expression data, we linked GMV asymmetry deviations in 1- to 7-year-old children to transcriptional pro /uniFB01 les from healthy adults ... Fourthly, the sex ratio of this work is unbalanced, which limits the exploration about sex effects on developmental disorders.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study used a multiscale cascade approach, linking macroscale brain imaging findings (GMV asymmetry) to behavioral/clinical phenotypes and microscale data (gene transcription profiles). It also differentiated between abnormalities in the mean deviation and the individual variability (kurtosis) of the deviations.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study makes a notable distinction between three groups: ASD with DD/ID, ASD without DD/ID, and DD/ID only, which allows for investigating the comorbidity and specificity of brain alterations. The use of normative modeling to generate individual deviation scores is key to moving beyond group-level case-control comparisons. There is a discrepancy in the number of TD subjects reported (219 in main text demographics vs. 247 for model training).
